target_customer: Drone manufacturers and commercial drone operators needing collision avoidance and detect and avoid for beyond line of sight flight
problem: Commercial drones could not safely see and avoid other aircraft, which blocked regulatory approval for BVLOS operations.
business_model: Hardware and software detect and avoid system sold to drone OEMs and operators (Casia)
product_category: Computer vision detect and avoid for drones

founders.name: Alexander Harmsen
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later co-founded PortfolioPilot and reports raising over 30M USD and approvals in 9 countries for Iris

competitors.name: Area17
competitors.what: SRI spin-out working on drone sense and avoid

competitors.name: Intel RealSense
competitors.what: Depth sensing technology used for obstacle avoidance

competitors.name: DJI Guidance
competitors.what: Obstacle sensing system for DJI drones

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time computer vision detection of distant aircraft on small drone hardware, which also needed regulatory validation.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms and regulatory approvals took years to replicate, but camera based approaches were pursued by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it early; uAvionix, an avionics firm owned by a private equity group, acquired it in October 2023.

market_need_then: Regulators required detect and avoid for BVLOS drone flights, and the company raised money in 2017 to build a turnkey system for commercial drone makers.

branding.domain_note: Company used irisonboard.com, now redirects to uAvionix (301).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the Casia product name continued under uAvionix.

outcome_analysis: Iris Automation built a computer vision detect and avoid system for commercial drones, raised a 1.5M seed in 2017, an 8M Series A in 2018 and a 13M Series B in 2020, and was acquired by uAvionix in October 2023. The exit price is not public. The company grew on a hard technical problem tied to regulatory demand for BVLOS flight, but a small market of drone operators and the long approval cycle made a standalone path difficult.
notes: Competitor names come from a search snippet attributed to a 2017 article that matches the TechCrunch seed coverage; the article text was not opened, so treat as medium reliability. BetaKit reported the Series A as 10M CAD while most outlets say 8M USD. Cumulative funding is reported as 22.5M or 25M by different sources. Founder education and prior employers not stated on the YC page; the company's team claim of NASA, Boeing and CV PhDs is not attributed to named people. A site fetch of irisonboard.com redirected to uAvionix. A search for acquisition by Zena Aero was a bad query and returned the uAvionix deal.
